_info: Dataset registry for the fence detector. Every dataset is synthetic and auto-labelled from Gazebo ground truth by tools/make_dataset.py (no hand labels). Images are not in git: they live on the training machine under ~/querra-data/<id> and can be regenerated with the command at the given code commit. Farm seed = --seed + layout number (default --seed 100), so layout 40 is always seed 140. Ids are the folder names. 'role' says how a split may be used: train, val (model selection) or test (never used for training or model selection).

datasets.notes: Random farms: fence shape, post spacing, wire heights, 2-3 broken wires, 1-2 fallen posts, 1-2 branches, herd, sun, grass colour. Camera 5-20 m, tilt 35-80 deg. The dead strand after a break is always grey.

datasets.command: tools/make_dataset.sh --style v2 (layouts 20-29, 300 frames; tests: layouts 40-42, 250 frames; --mission-world layout 90, 400 frames)
datasets.notes: Targets the false broken wire: 3-4 breaks per farm, so long dead strands, drawn in random colours (grey, live yellow, dull, dark) and labelled wire. Three break shapes. 60% of the poses imitate the inspection flight.

datasets.command: tools/make_dataset.sh --seed 100 --look rich --style v3 --start 200 --layouts 212 --split train --frames 300 (val: --start 212 --layouts 214; test: --style v2 --start 40 --layouts 43 --frames 250; mission: --mission-world --start 90 --layouts 91 --frames 400)
datasets.notes: The rich world (textured grass, terrain, sky): random sun height and strength, sky fill, ambient light, grass tint, one terrain mesh per farm. The test farms use the same seeds as fence_yolo_v2's test, so the two looks are compared on the same farms and pose distribution (not frame-identical: empty frames are skipped).
Classic look with the v3 poses: v2 plus 20% low re-fly hovers (4.5-8 m, pitch 48-62 deg, mostly at faults).
Close-ups like the re-fly hover (about 6 m), to score the verification step.
The same farms and poses as fence_yolo_refly_classic, in the rich look.

datasets.command: tools/cam_record.py during ./start.sh (the default mission over fence.json)
datasets.notes: The JPEG stream the Jetson receives (tools/cam_stream.py, 640x400), with the simulator's GPS and heading per frame. No boxes: tools/eval_mission.py scores it against the three known faults (F1-F3). The same recording is the ROS 2 replay demo on the Jetson (/ssd/querra/sim/m1).
